newsitem.title: USA: U.S. inflation well in check for now - Labor Dept.
newsitem.headline: U.S. inflation well in check for now - Labor Dept.

text.p: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics economist Patrick Jackman said on Tuesday that inflation remained well in check, but the 1.4 percent annualized rate so far this year was unlikely to be sustained.
Jackman also told Reuters Financial Television that seasonal adjustment factors, which had helped the Consumer Price Index stay low in the first part of the year, would no longer be as helpful.
"I certainly would concur that inflation remains well in check, the numbers I think just exceed everybody's expectation at this time," Jackman said.
"I guess I would add one point of caution here that the seasonal factors, particularly in the volatile components, food and energy, have helped us so far this year," he said.
"I don't think anybody looks at the 1.4 (pct annual rate so far) for the CPI and sees that as the rate that we're going to end up at the end of year."
"The seasonal factors are no longer going to help us in the food and the energy area, at least in the short run here," Jackman said.
